lessons.title: Running a Game
lessons.blurb: Clock, field, weather and the roster.

steps.title: Clock management
steps.body: Timeouts, the two-minute warning, spikes, kneels and out-of-bounds throws are resources. Use free stoppages before timeouts, and think a full drive ahead.

steps.title: Home field and weather
steps.body: Home-field advantage is real but smaller than it used to be. Wind hurts passing and kicking more than cold or rain, which can change 4th-down and field-goal choices.

steps.title: Roster and the cap
steps.body: Each NFL team has a hard salary cap. Players on rookie contracts are cheap for their value, which is why a good young quarterback lets a team spend more around him. Releasing a player can still leave 'dead money' on the cap.

steps.prompt: Strong wind is blowing straight across the field. Which plays get riskier?
choices: Long passes and long field goals
steps.explanation: Wind pushes deep balls and long kicks; the run game barely notices.

steps.prompt: Why is a quarterback on a rookie contract such an advantage?
choices: His low salary leaves cap room to build the roster
The cap doesn't apply to them
steps.explanation: A cheap starting quarterback frees money for the rest of the team.

steps.statement: Releasing a player can still count against the salary cap.
steps.explanation: Guaranteed money already paid or owed becomes dead money on the cap.
